title: The star cluster NGC 2100 in context
caption: The star cluster NGC 2100 and the Tarantula Nebula, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope
celestial: NGC 2100, Tarantula Nebula · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This wide view shows the neighbourhood of the star cluster NGC 2100, which lies in the Large Magellanic Cloud, a small companion galaxy of the Milky Way. The cluster is only part of the story, since the Tarantula Nebula dominates the frame.

The Tarantula is the most active star-forming region in the Local Group, the collection of galaxies that includes the Milky Way. Star-forming regions are vast clouds of gas and dust where gravity pulls material together into new stars, and the young, hot stars that result light up the gas around them.

Putting NGC 2100 in context like this helps show how clusters and nebulae share the same galactic neighbourhood. The picture was assembled from visible-light exposures made with the Wide Field Imager, the camera mounted on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope. Its wide field lets it take in the cluster and the sprawling nebula in a single frame.
scale: The source lists a distance of 170000 light years, so the light in this picture set out roughly 170,000 years ago.

understand.summary: The Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope recorded this scene in visible light through blue, visual, oxygen and hydrogen-alpha filters. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye, and the gas filters isolate the glow of particular elements.

explore: The region lies about 170,000 light-years away. The camera used blue, visual, oxygen and hydrogen-alpha filters, the last two picking out light from glowing gas.
alt: A wide field dominated by the Tarantula Nebula, which surrounds the star cluster NGC 2100.
